Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto centres on economic stability, citing reduced inflation (from 11.1% to 2.3%), returning growth, and rising real wages. Key tax proposals include:

- Halving employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027
- Abolishing the main rate of self-employed National Insurance
- Introducing a "Triple Lock Plus" for pensioners, guaranteeing the State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowance rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%
- Maintaining current rates of income tax, VAT, and Capital Gains Tax
- Reforming Child Benefit to a household basis, with thresholds set at £120,000-£160,000

The manifesto commits to meeting fiscal rules requiring falling public sector net debt and borrowing below 3% of GDP.

## Immigration

Proposals include:

- Introducing a legally binding annual cap on migration
- Continuing deportation flights to Rwanda for illegal migrants
- Working to reform international asylum treaties
- Raising visa salary thresholds and health requirements for migrants

## Public Services

**NHS**: Commitments include above-inflation funding increases annually, recruiting 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors, expanding Pharmacy First, building 250 GP surgeries, and 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.

**Education**: Plans include mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (military or civic), 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing underperforming university courses, banning mobile phones in schools during the school day, and introducing the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education.

## Housing and Infrastructure

- Target of 1.6 million new homes in England
- Abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules to unlock 100,000 homes
- Permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on homes up to £425,000
- New Help to Buy scheme
- £36 billion transport investment from cancelled HS2 phase two, including £8.3 billion for roads

## Defence and Security

- Increasing defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030
- Continued support for Ukraine
- Investment in nuclear deterrent and new defence technologies
- £10 billion investment in UK munitions production

## Energy and Environment

- Annual licensing rounds for North Sea oil and gas
- Trebling offshore wind capacity
- Building new nuclear capacity including Small Modular Reactors
- Commitment to net zero by 2050 with a "pragmatic" approach
- No new green levies on household bills

## Welfare Reform

- Reforming disability benefits assessment
- Tightening work capability assessments
- Introducing sanctions removing benefits after 12 months for those refusing suitable work
- Projected savings of £12 billion annually

## Devolution and Union

The manifesto commits to maintaining the UK internal market, extending levelling up funding across Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, and opposing Scottish independence while implementing the Windsor Framework commitments for Northern Ireland.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS expenditure by 2030, plus £20bn capital spending over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteed rapid GP access, NHS dentistry for all (£3bn/year by 2030), boosted staff pay, restored public health budgets, and a National Cancer Plan. Mental health services would receive investment for 28-day therapy access. The party opposes NHS privatisation.

## Social Care
Proposals include free personal care (similar to Scotland's model), increased carer pay with career structures, and £20bn annual investment. Disability benefits would increase 5%, and £3bn additional funding would support children's social care.

## Housing
The party proposes 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils for rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and a £29bn five-year home insulation programme. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include infrastructure.

## Energy and Climate
Proposals include wind providing 70% of electricity by 2030, no new oil/gas licences, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and community energy ownership. A carbon tax starting at £120/tonne would rise to £500/tonne within ten years. Nuclear development would cease.

## Economy and Work
The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual green investment, bringing water companies, railways, and major energy retailers into public ownership. A £15/hour minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, repeal of anti-union legislation, and movement toward a four-day week are proposed.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase £40/week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, and the five-week benefit wait would end. Pensions would maintain inflation-linked rises, and carer's allowance would increase 10%.

## Taxation
Proposals include a 1% wealth tax on assets over £10m (2% over £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, and removing the upper earnings limit on National Insurance. Estimated additional revenue: £50-70bn annually by parliament's end.

## Environment and Nature
A Rights of Nature Act would give nature legal personhood. 30% of land and seas would be protected by 2030. Water companies would return to public ownership. Harmful pesticides including glyphosate would be phased out, and a new Right to Roam Act would be introduced.

## Education
School funding would increase £8bn (including £2bn teacher pay uplift). £2.5bn annually would address building safety. Tuition fees would be scrapped and maintenance grants restored. £5bn would fund SEND provision.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, with free bus travel for under-18s. Railways would return to public ownership. £2.5bn annually would fund cycleways and footpaths. Petrol/diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027.

## Democracy
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, an elected second chamber replacing the House of Lords, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The party proposes ending the hostile environment, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work during applications, and removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas.

## Foreign Policy
Commitments include an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, Palestinian state recognition, ending UK arms exports to Israel, increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI (rising to 1.5% for climate finance by 2033), and working toward EU rejoinment. The party would sign the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and cancel Trident replacement.
